name: MS-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: Guest's cash advantage of roughly $963K to $23K
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 98%
No polls or expert ratings; Libertarian on ballot adds minor uncertainty
model.rationale: A fourteen-point Republican district, a well-funded incumbent, and markets pricing a Republican win near certainty leave Guest firmly favored; Chiaradio's modest war chest offers no evident path to close the gap.
model.watch: A late wave of outside Democratic spending or an unusually favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains a long shot.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mississippi's 3rd District leans firmly Republican, and incumbent Michael Guest returns with the advantages of holding a safe seat. He has raised more than $820,000 and holds roughly $960,000 in cash, while Democratic nominee Michael Chiaradio has raised about $155,000 with just $23,000 on hand. A Libertarian candidate, Erik Kiehle, also appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 98 percent. The district's fourteen-point Republican lean, combined with Guest's incumbency and financial edge, leaves Chiaradio with little evident path. The main open question is the size of the Republican margin, which national political conditions could nudge in either direction without changing the likely outcome.
